examples.question_text: A bushwalker walks $5$ km from $A$ to $B$ on a bearing of $060^{\circ}\text{T}$. Find how far east $B$ is from $A$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A vehicle travels $8$ km from $A$ to $B$ on a bearing of $155^{\circ}\text{T}$. It then travels due north until it is due east of $A$. Find the distance it travels north, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A helicopter flies $9$ km on a bearing of $150^{\circ}\text{T}$, then flies $2$ km due east. How far east of its starting point is it, correct to $1$ decimal place?

A ship sails $6$ km from $O$ to $P$ on a bearing of $040^{\circ}\text{T}$, then $8$ km from $P$ to $Q$ on a bearing of $130^{\circ}\text{T}$. Find (a) its distance from $O$ and (b) the bearing of $Q$ from $O$, to the nearest degree.

A walker travels $9$ km due north from $O$ to $P$, then $12$ km due east to a shelter $Q$. Find (a) the bearing of $Q$ from $O$ and (b) the bearing of $O$ from $Q$. Give both bearings to the nearest degree.

A helicopter flies $5$ km from town $T$ to depot $D$ on a bearing of $315^{\circ}\text{T}$. It then flies to site $C$ on a bearing of $225^{\circ}\text{T}$. The site is $13$ km from $T$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $T$, to the nearest degree.

Two ships leave harbour $H$ together. One travels at $8$ km/h on a bearing of $030^{\circ}\text{T}$ and the other at $6$ km/h on a bearing of $120^{\circ}\text{T}$. How far apart are they after $3$ hours?

examples.derivation: The reference angle from east is 90°−60°=30°. Thus x=5 cos30°=4.330127… km, giving 4.33 km east.
The reference angle from south is 180°−155°=25°. The southward component is 8 cos25°=7.250462… km, so the required northward return is 7.25 km.

The first leg makes 30° with south. Its eastward component is 9 sin30°=4.5 km. Adding 2 km east gives 6.5 km. The diagram preserves the directions and right-triangle relationships; its journey lengths are schematic.

The reverse bearing PO is 220°, giving angle OPQ = 220° − 130° = 90°. Hence OQ = sqrt(6² + 8²) = 10 km. At O, tan(theta) = 8/6, so theta = 53.130102…°. OQ lies clockwise from OP, giving bearing 40° + 53.130102…° = 93.130102…°, rounded to 093°T. Diagram coordinates reproduce the two bearings and the 6:8 length ratio within coordinate rounding; the right-angle marker and theta arc match the working.
The clockwise angle from north is arctan(12/9)=53.130102…°, giving 053°T. The reverse direction is 233.130102…°, giving 233°T.

The bearing of T from D is 135°, so angle TDC=225°−135°=90°. With adjacent side 5 km and hypotenuse 13 km, θ=arccos(5/13)=67.380135…°. The endpoint lies anticlockwise from TD, giving 315°−67.380135…°=247.619864…°, rounded to 248°T.
After 3 hours the distances are 24 km and 18 km. Their bearings differ by 90°, so separation is √(24²+18²)=30 km.
